(a) 
Title 10, United States Code, is amended as follows:

        (1) Section 101 is amended by adding the following new clause:


“(36) 
‘Dependent’, with respect to a female member of an armed force, does not include her husband, unless he is in fact dependent on her for his chief support, or her child, unless his father is dead or he is in fact dependent on her for his chief support.”



 
        (2) Chapter 53 is amended—

            (A) 
by adding the following new section:


“§ 1040. 
Replacement of certificate of discharge
“If satisfactory proof is presented that a person who was discharged honorably or under honorable conditions has lost his certificate of discharge from an armed force or that it was destroyed without his procurement or connivance, the Secretary concerned may give that person, or his surviving spouse, a certificate of that discharge, indelibly marked to show that it is a certificate in place of the lost or destroyed certificate. A certificate given under this section may not be accepted as a voucher for the payment of a claim against the United States for pay, bounty, or other allowance, or as evidence in any other case.”; and



 
            (B) 
by adding the following new item at the end of the analysis:


“1040. Replacement of certificate of discharge.”



  
        (3) 
Sections 3685, 3693, 6033, 8685, and 8693 are repealed.
 
        (4) 
The analysis of chapter 353 is amended by striking out the following items:


“3685. Regular Army; Army Reserve: female members; definition of ‘dependents’.


“*      *      *      *      *      *      *


“3693. Replacement of certificate of discharge.”



 
        (5) 
The analysis of chapter 555 is amended by striking out the following item:


“6033. Woman member: definition of dependents.”



 
        (6) 
The analysis of chapter 853 is amended by striking out the following items:


“8685. Regular Air Force; Air Force Reserve: female members; definition of ‘dependents’.


“*      *      *      *      *      *      *


“8693. Replacement of certificates of discharge.”



  
    (b) 
Title 10, United States Code, is amended as follows:

        (1)

        (3)

“3690. Exemption from arrest for debt: enlisted members.”



 
        (4)

“6158. Exemption from arrest for debt: enlisted members of Marine Corps.”



 
        (5)

“8690. Exemption from arrest for debt: enlisted members.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a person presenting proof to the Secretary is an outside party taking part in a federal decision. That is only an individual request for a replacement document, which is akin to an application for a benefit, not consultation on a policy decision. The rest of the section defines 'dependent' and makes technical repeals and analysis amendments to Title 10, with no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, outside consultation, or right to sue.

qwen_block.w: This section amends Title 10 to define dependents and establish a process for replacing lost discharge certificates. These are administrative procedures for military personnel and their families, not mechanisms for outside parties to participate in federal decision-making. There is no consultation, public hearing, advisory board with non-federal members, or right to sue involved.
qwen_block.s: “§ 1040. Replacement of certificate of discharge “If satisfactory proof is presented that a person who was discharged honorably or under honorable conditions has lost his certificate of discharge from an armed force or that it was destroyed without his procurement or connivance, the Secretary concerned may give that person, or his surviving spouse, a certificate of that discharge, indelibly marked to show that it is a certificate in place of the lost or destroyed certificate.

opus.w: The only interaction with an outside party is a person submitting proof to get a replacement discharge certificate. That works like an application for an individual benefit, which the definition excludes. The rest of the section amends definitions, repeals sections and edits chapter tables of contents. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation or right to sue.
opus.s: If satisfactory proof is presented that a person who was discharged honorably or under honorable conditions has lost his certificate of discharge from an armed force or that it was destroyed without his procurement or connivance, the Secretary concerned may give that person, or his surviving spouse, a certificate of that discharge
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** In the new § 1040, a former service member, or their surviving spouse, presents "satisfactory proof" that a discharge certificate was lost. That looks like an outside person interacting with the Secretary before a federal decision. It fails the definition because this is a request for an individual document, like applying for a benefit. It is not consultation on a federal policy decision. Nothing else in the section involves outside parties: the rest is definitions, repeals and edits to chapter tables of contents.

2. **Answer:**

qwen_chat.w: This section primarily deals with internal military definitions (dependents) and administrative procedures for replacing lost documents. The provision allowing a person to receive a replacement certificate is an application for a benefit/document, which the definition explicitly excludes from participation. There is no consultation with outside parties, public hearings, or advisory committees involving non-federal members in the decision-making process described here.
qwen_chat.s: “§ 1040. Replacement of certificate of discharge “If satisfactory proof is presented that a person who was discharged honorably or under honorable conditions has lost his certificate of discharge from an armed force or that it was destroyed without his procurement or connivance, the Secretary concerned may give that person, or his surviving spouse, a certificate of that discharge...
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the section involves "participation" because it allows individuals (veterans, spouses) to apply for a replacement certificate of discharge. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits or grants" are not participation. Furthermore, the rest of the section deals with internal military definitions and repeals, which are purely internal government matters.
